newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees higher December sales.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees higher December sales.

text.p: Ford Motor Co Group Vice President Robert Rewey said the automaker expects to report an increase in U.S. vehicle sales for the month of December.

In an interview at the Los Angeles Auto Show, Rewey said he expected December car sales to be flat with the year ago level but truck sales should be up sharply. Ford, the nation's second- largest automaker, is scheduled to report December sales figures on Monday.

Rewey said poor weather in the U.S. Northwest and midwest may have hurt sales temporarily, but the drop is not expected to last long. For 1997, Rewey expects U.S. industry sales to be about 15.1 million to 15.4 million vehicles, about the same as last year's level.

Ross Roberts, general manager of Ford Motor Co's Ford Division, said truck sales were "fantastic" in December and should easily top the year-ago period. Ford division's car sales should be slightly better than the year ago. For the full year, Roberts said Ford should sell more than two million trucks, minivans and sport utility vehicles, a new record.

The Ford executives were on hand to unveil a new concept car called the "L'attitude", a cross between a sport utility vehicle and a station wagon and discuss plans for the introduction of a new sport utility vehicle for the Lincoln brand called the "Navigator."
Jim O'Connor, general manager of the Lincoln Mercury division, said the Navigator will be an important part of Ford's strategy to lure younger buyers to the Lincoln Brand.
The Navigator will be unveiled in Detroit next week.
"We're really looking forward to Navigator expanding the scope of Lincoln," he said. "The full size sport utility market is really starting to boom."
